title: Q-Shaped Options for Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
abstract: arXiv:2610.12135v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Learning to tackle long-horizon, goal-conditioned tasks requires an agent to reason over extended timescales and act across a broad range of states. In principle, Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (HRL) addresses both challenges through the interaction between action (temporal) and state (spatial) abstraction. First, using an action abstraction to represent temporally extended behaviour as options reduces the effective decision horizon. Second, enabling different state abstractions at each level of the decision process permits greater data aggregation for learning. However, realising these two benefits of a hierarchical policy depends on learning an appropriate action abstraction. Current HRL algorithms fail in one of two ways. Some discard distinctions between options needed for optimal control, undermining hierarchy altogether. translated_title: 面向分层强化学习的Q塑形选项
translated_abstract: 学习解决长时程、目标条件任务，需要智能体能够在扩展的时间尺度上进行推理，并在广泛的状态范围内采取行动。原则上，分层强化学习（HRL）通过动作（时间）抽象与状态（空间）抽象之间的相互作用来应对这两个挑战。首先，使用动作抽象将时间上延伸的行为表示为选项，可以缩短有效的决策时域；其次，在决策过程的每个层级允许不同的状态抽象，可以为学习带来更大程度的数据聚合。然而，要实现分层策略的这两个好处，关键在于学习到合适的动作抽象。当前的HRL算法往往会以两种方式之一失败：一类算法丢弃了最优控制所需的选项之间的区分，从而彻底破坏了分层结构；另一类算法则保留了不必要的区分，虽然维持了决策时域的缩短，却放弃了更粗粒度的状态抽象。
tldr: 提出基于Q值塑形的选项（Q-Shaped Options），使分层强化学习在通过动作抽象缩短决策时域的同时，保留最优控制所需的选项区分，从而兼容更粗粒度的状态抽象。
en_tdlr: Proposes Q-shaped options that preserve the option distinctions necessary for optimal control while enabling coarser state abstractions, allowing hierarchical reinforcement learning to jointly benefit from horizon reduction and spatial abstraction.
